response: Yes, limb-salvage surgery often offers patients better quality of life and functional capacity than amputation. This is because it allows patients to retain their natural limb, which can lead to improved mobility, reduced risk of complications, and enhanced overall well-being. Additionally, advancements in surgical techniques and rehabilitation methods have significantly improved the outcomes of limb-salvage surgery, enabling patients to regain functional ability and participate in daily activities with greater ease. However, the decision between limb-salvage surgery and amputation ultimately depends on individual patient factors, such as the extent of tissue damage, overall health, and personal preferences.
